title: Isolation of human fetal intestinal cells for single-cell RNA sequencing
author: Fawkner-Corbett, Gerós, et al.

steps.title: Prepare required buffers
steps.instruction: Make Transport medium, HPGA, Wash medium, Chelation medium, Thaw medium, and Buffer L replacement according to the recipe.

steps.title: Set water bath temperature
steps.instruction: Adjust the water bath to 37 °C and allow it to equilibrate.

steps.title: Set centrifuges to 4 °C
steps.instruction: Place two benchtop centrifuges at 4 °C: one for 50 mL and 15 mL tubes, the other for 1.5 mL vials. All centrifugation steps will be at 300 g, 4 °C for 4 min.

steps.title: Pre‑freeze cryopreserved tissue
steps.instruction: If using cryopreserved tissue, move the samples to a –80 °C freezer and keep them there for at least 1 hour before further processing.

steps.title: Thaw fetal bovine serum aliquot
steps.instruction: Thaw a 50 mL aliquot of sterile‑filtered fetal bovine serum (FBS).

steps.title: Dispense Buffer L into 24‑well plate
steps.instruction: For each sample, add 700 µL Buffer L replacement to one well and 2 mL Buffer L replacement to a second well of a 24‑well plate; then place the plate in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Prepare tissue for chelation
steps.instruction: Process tissue according to its preservation state before chelation.

substeps.instruction: Fresh tissue: centrifuge tissue fragments in transport medium; aspirate medium; add 3 mL ACK lysing buffer, shake, and incubate at room temperature (18‑22 °C) for 5 min; add 10 mL wash medium and centrifuge; aspirate wash medium; repeat the 10 mL wash and centrifugation once more; then continue to the next step.

Frozen tissue: in a 50 mL tube add 25 mL thaw medium; keep samples on ice while transporting from –80 °C; thaw in a 37 °C water bath for ~2 min until only small ice crystals remain; add thaw medium to fill the cryovial, mix three times, and transfer the contents to the tube with 25 mL thaw medium; agitate and centrifuge; aspirate thaw medium and wash tissue with 10 mL wash medium; then continue to the next step.

steps.title: Replace wash with chelation medium
steps.instruction: Aspirate the final wash medium and add 10 mL pre‑warmed chelation medium to each tube.

steps.title: First chelation incubation and collect fraction 1
steps.instruction: Shake the tube and incubate in a 37 °C water bath for 15 min, vortexing or shaking every 5 min for 5‑10 s; after the final vortex let the tissue settle, then transfer the supernatant to a new 15 mL tube (crypt fraction 1) using an FBS‑coated pipette and keep on ice. (Leave ~500 µL chelation medium in the tissue for later steps.)

steps.title: Second chelation and collect fraction 2
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL fresh chelation medium to the tissue tube and repeat the 15‑min chelation incubation, vortex schedule, and supernatant collection as in step 9 to obtain crypt fraction 2. While this incubation proceeds, centrifuge crypt fraction 1 and resuspend the pellet in 2 mL cold transport medium in a 15 mL tube; keep on ice. After the second incubation, pool crypt fraction 2 with fraction 1 (total ≈4 mL transport medium) on ice.

steps.title: Third chelation, prepare enzymes, pool fractions
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL chelation medium for a third 15‑min incubation, following the same vortexing and collection to obtain crypt fraction 3. During the breaks between chelation steps, prepare the stromal digestion enzyme mix as described later. After collecting fraction 3, pool all three crypt fractions (≈6 mL) in a 15 mL tube and centrifuge.

steps.title: Transfer remaining tissue to stromal digestion
steps.instruction: Aspirate all remaining chelation medium from the residual tissue and move the tissue directly into the stromal digestion cocktail in the incubator.

steps.title: Digest crypts with TrypLE and DNAse
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pooled crypt fractions in 3 mL warm TrypLE Express containing 50 µg/mL DNAse; place the tube in a 37 °C incubator and incubate for 35 min with continuous agitation or rotation (e.g., MACSmix). Move the remaining crypt‑depleted tissue straight into the stromal digestion cocktail using a blow‑out pipette as prepared in step 11.
